create.name: Buddhist Discussion Centre Australia
create.bio:
The Buddhist Discussion Centre Australia is a small Buddhist temple in Upwey, in the Dandenong Ranges on Melbourne's outer eastern edge, started in 1978 by lay people as a self-help group run without profit. It describes itself as home-grown and Australian rather than tied to one school, so its teaching draws on Theravada and Mahayana sources as well as Vajrayana and Chan, or Zen. The spiritual director and abbot is Anita Carter, who came to the centre as a student in 1996; with her husband Frank Carter, a resident teacher and long-time leader of the centre, she wrote the book Bringing Wisdom To Life from forty years of talks there. It acts as one of the World Fellowship of Buddhists' regional centres.

Each week there is a free Saturday evening class of teaching and meditation, led by a visiting monk or nun or by resident lay teachers, and a Sunday afternoon class as well, with a practice day on the last Saturday of every month. Six-week introductory workshops run several times a year, and Chan painting and sumi-e brush classes are offered as a meditative art. Members of the centre also present the Buddhist Hour on local community radio each Sunday and run an online station of talks and chanting.

courses.title: Membership
courses.description: Membership of the centre, giving access to all its activities and resources, voting at general meetings, regular newsletters and, after a year or two, the chance to propose motions or hold office. Library use and Chan or sumi-e painting classes are charged separately.

courses.title: Chan Painting & Sumi-e Classes
courses.description: Brush-and-ink painting taught as a Chan (Zen) practice that trains the mind through ink, paper, ink-slab and brush.

free_resources.title: Weekly Teaching and Meditation Classes
free_resources.description: Free weekly classes at the Upwey temple: a Saturday evening session of Buddhist teaching and meditation led by a visiting monk or nun or a resident lay teacher, and a Sunday afternoon Dhamma and meditation class, plus a monthly practice day.

free_resources.title: Online Meditation Sessions
free_resources.description: Recorded guided meditations to use at home: mindfulness of breathing with Bhante Kassapa, a loving-kindness (metta) instruction by Venerable Mahinda, a morning chanting and metta practice led by Anita Carter with its chanting sheet, and an instruction video on walking meditation.

free_resources.title: World Buddhist Radio and Buddhist Hour
free_resources.description: The centre's round-the-clock internet station of Dhamma talks, sutta readings and chanting, together with an archive of transcripts from its weekly Buddhist Hour programme on Melbourne community radio.
